memos.headline: Parabolic Leaders S05/S02/S07 Flash Overbought Signals While Laggards S01/S06 Show Persistent Relative Weakness
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape as of May 1. The strongest momentum names—S05 (RSI 82.5, +30.4% in 4w, 22% above 50d), S02 (RSI 82.7, +33% in 4w, 22% above 50d), and S07 (RSI 75, +24% in 4w, 50% above 200d)—are all at or near 52-week highs with extreme extensions that historically precede mean-reversion pullbacks of at least one ATR. I would wait for a pullback toward the 50d mean before adding to S07 or S10, and I would outright avoid chasing S05 and S02 at these RSI levels. On the weak side, S01 sits 13% off its high, below both moving averages, with negative 12w relative strength of -11% vs SPY—a clear downtrend I want no part of. S08 is the cleanest setup: only 2% off its high, RSI 66 (strong but not overbought), above both averages, with moderate extension; a close below the 50d mean (~261) would change my view.

views.note: Healthy uptrend only 2% off highs with RSI 66 and manageable 7% extension above 50d; invalidated on a close below ~261.
Above both MAs with strong 12w relative strength vs SPY (+8.9%), RSI 53 leaves room to run; would cut below ~187 (200d area).
Dominant trend (+71% in 26w, +24% rel strength) but 50% above 200d and RSI 75 screams overextension—wait for a pullback toward ~750 before entry.
RSI 82.5 and 37% above 200d is parabolic; despite sitting at highs, risk/reward is poor for new longs at this extension.
RSI 82.7 with +33% in 4w is the most stretched name in the universe; still 9% off 52w high suggesting prior distribution—dangerous setup.
Below both moving averages, -13% drawdown, -11% 12w relative strength vs SPY—clear underperformer with no sign of a bottom.
Low vol (ATR 1.8%) and mild RSI 58 but negative 12w relative strength (-6.5% vs SPY) and below-average momentum keep me sidelined.
Bouncing +11% in 4w but still 23.5% off highs and 11% below 200d—this is a bear-market rally until price reclaims ~460.
At 52w highs with RSI 78 and 19% above 50d; trend is powerful but extension is extreme—prefer to buy a pullback toward ~240.
RSI 49 and sitting right at the 50d mean with -15% 4w relative strength vs SPY; momentum has stalled despite a strong 26w return.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Collapse
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 delivered a 63.1% net margin on $68.1B of revenue with only $8.5B in total debt and 94.5% YoY net income growth—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly impressive at 56.9% net margin, +81.2% YoY net income growth, and minimal leverage ($14.8B debt on $109.9B revenue). On the other end, S02 posted near-zero net income ($0.01B) on $113.2B of revenue despite 12.3% top-line growth, implying severe cost or impairment issues that destroyed earnings power. S09 is shrinking revenue (-1.3% YoY) with a thin 7.9% margin and 14.6% net income decline, while carrying $34.2B in debt—a combination I refuse to pay for. S04 and S03 sit in a constructive middle ground: S04's 38.3% margin and 23.1% earnings growth are durable, while S03's 76.7% net income surge is eye-catching but the 16.7% margin and $122.6B debt load temper my enthusiasm until I see margin expansion sustain.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, near-zero leverage ($8.5B debt), and 94.5% YoY net income growth represent best-in-class earnings power; a margin decline below 50% would change my view.
56.9% net margin with 81.2% YoY net income growth and only $14.8B debt on $109.9B revenue is outstanding; I'd reassess if margin compresses below 45%.
38.3% net margin and 23.1% earnings growth on manageable $40.3B debt make this a durable compounder; revenue deceleration below 10% YoY would be a warning.
Solid 29.3% margin and 15.7% revenue growth but $88.5B in total debt is meaningful; need to see leverage stabilize or decline before getting more constructive.
76.7% YoY net income growth is impressive but 16.7% margin and $122.6B debt suggest the earnings surge may reflect one-time items rather than structural improvement.
28.4% margin is decent but $435.2B in total debt dwarfs the $13.0B net income, and earnings declined 7% YoY—leverage trajectory is the key variable.
18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are steady but unexciting; $23.9B debt on $21.2B quarterly revenue warrants monitoring.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% YoY and 12.5% margin with $36.2B debt on $19.1B revenue signals margin pressure; need to see earnings inflect.
Near-zero net income ($0.01B) on $113.2B revenue with $78.4B debt and a 99.8% YoY earnings collapse is a clear avoid until margin recovery is demonstrated.
Revenue declining 1.3% YoY, net income down 14.6%, thin 7.9% margin, and $34.2B debt—this is textbook cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.3% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensive Positioning
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months despite 75bp of cuts over the past year, and the effective rate at 3.64% confirms no movement. The problem is inflation: CPI is running 3.3% YoY and 1.3% over just the last three months (roughly 5.3% annualized), which is well above target and likely keeps the Fed sidelined or even hawkish in tone. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10bp over three months, so there is no urgency to ease further. Meanwhile, the 10y yield has risen 13bp over three months to 4.39% and the 2s10s curve has flattened 22bp to just 52bp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and potentially slower growth. A CPI print that drops below 3.0% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.5% would change my regime call from 'hawkish pause' to 'easing resumption.'

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds as 10y yields grind higher and the Fed stays on hold with sticky inflation.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (52bp 2s10s) and stable rates; net interest margins should hold up in this pause regime.
Staples offer defensive value as the macro mix of sticky inflation and flattening curve points to late-cycle caution.
Energy is a mixed bag—stable labor market supports demand but rising real rates and slowing growth expectations cap upside.
Cyclicals look vulnerable as the curve flattens sharply and higher-for-longer rates weigh on forward growth expectations.
Insufficient macro catalyst to take a strong view; the pause regime and stable unemployment leave this name range-bound.

memos.headline: Earnings-Season Sentiment Divergence: S05 and S07 Pop Hard While S04 Sinks on Results
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. S05 (+10.0%) and S07 (+9.9%) both surged on their 4/29-4/30 results filings, suggesting a sharp positive narrative shift that may still have momentum if media tone follows. S02 (+7.0% on 4/21) and S08 (+3.2% on 4/30) also printed positive reactions, though the magnitude is smaller and some of that move may already be priced. On the negative side, S04 dropped -3.9% on its 4/29 results, a clear sentiment deterioration, while S06 slipped -0.8% on its mid-April print and has since filed governance-related 8-Ks (bylaws amendment) that add uncertainty. S10 has had two director departure/appointment filings in recent months with no earnings catalyst yet, leaving its narrative ambiguous and uninformative from a sentiment standpoint.

views.note: Three consecutive director-change filings followed by a +10.0% earnings pop signals a strong positive narrative inflection.
A +9.9% one-day reaction to Q results is a decisive sentiment shift upward that likely has not fully been absorbed by broader media.
The +7.0% earnings-day move on 4/21 was strong, but it is now 10 days old and some of the positive tone may already be priced.
A +3.2% post-earnings move is modestly positive but a recent director change adds governance noise that tempers conviction.
A -3.9% drop on results is a clear negative sentiment signal with no offsetting positive catalysts in the filing flow.
Mildly negative earnings reaction (-0.8%) compounded by a bylaws amendment filing suggests governance uncertainty and no positive narrative.
Two director-change filings with no earnings catalyst leave the sentiment picture too ambiguous to act on.
A +1.7% earnings reaction is tepid and the dual Reg FD filings suggest management is actively managing narrative, which cuts both ways.
High filing volume (five 8-Ks in two months) but only a +0.8% earnings reaction implies the market had already priced the narrative.
No earnings filing yet and only routine Other Events / Reg FD disclosures leave no actionable sentiment signal.

memos.headline: Surging Oil and Elevated Policy Uncertainty Signal Structural Geopolitical Risk Despite VIX Compression
memos.body: I see a deeply bifurcated risk picture as of today. WTI crude at $108.64/bbl is up 68.4% over three months, a move consistent with a major supply disruption or escalating energy-security tensions rather than a demand-driven rally. Simultaneously, the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 386.28, up 82.7% over three months, indicating that policy actions—likely sanctions, export controls, or trade restrictions—are driving structural uncertainty even as the VIX has collapsed 44.8% in the past month, suggesting equity markets may be complacent relative to the underlying geopolitical stress. The flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread down 22bp over three months to 0.52pp) and only modestly wider HY spreads (+3bp over 3m) reinforce my view that credit markets are not yet pricing the tail risk embedded in the energy and policy data. I have higher conviction on names with direct energy exposure or supply-chain concentration risk, and lower conviction where I lack company-specific geopolitical detail.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate communication, possibly navigating policy or regulatory developments, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.

Three 8-K filings including a Reg FD on April 30 suggest the company is actively managing market communication amid elevated uncertainty, but I lack specifics to differentiate from the broader risk environment.

With policy uncertainty near historic highs and oil surging, any name with significant input-cost or supply-chain exposure faces margin risk; S06's April filings may reflect early disclosure of such pressures.
Two Reg FD filings in April suggest proactive investor communication, but without content I cannot assess whether the company benefits from or is harmed by the current geopolitical regime.

The 68% three-month oil surge and elevated policy uncertainty create headwinds for companies exposed to energy costs or trade restrictions; S09's March-April filings may reflect early positioning around these risks.
Only one Reg FD filing in March provides insufficient signal; the macro backdrop is hostile but I have no company-specific geopolitical exposure data.

plan.summary: Overweight the highest-quality fundamental names (S10, S08) that also have manageable technical extension, while keeping a moderate position in S05 for its exceptional earnings power despite stretched technicals. Hold significant cash (~42%) given sticky inflation, rising long rates, surging oil, and extreme overbought readings across several momentum leaders.

plans.rationale: Best-in-class fundamentals (63.1% net margin, 94.5% earnings growth, near-zero leverage) with a technically constructive setup: RSI 53 leaves ample room, above both MAs, and +8.9% 12w relative strength. Fundamentals analyst (0.95) and Technical analyst (0.55) both favor it.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below the 200-day moving average (~187) or net margin falling below 50% in the next quarterly report.

plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 50-day mean (~261) would invalidate the trend structure.

plans.rationale: Exceptional fundamentals (56.9% margin, 81.2% earnings growth) and strong positive sentiment (+10% earnings pop) justify exposure, but RSI 82.5 and 37% above 200d force a reduced size. Fundamentals (0.90) and Sentiment (0.75) are strongly bullish; Technical analyst warns of parabolic extension.

Sized small to reflect the disagreement between Fundamentals/Macro (bullish) and Sentiment/Technical (bearish).
